Laila — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a concise MAP and attached the first draft (Pioneer_MAP_v1.2.xlsx). Highlights below:

1) Evaluation windows (2-week cadence):
   - Week 0: Provision AWS private offer (placeholder PO) + shared test dataset setup
   - Week 1: Latency/throughput smoke tests (10K QPS overlay for peak candidate routes)
   - Week 2: Feature gating and integration tests with Pioneer ingestion pipeline

2) Technical acceptance gates (deliverables for sign-off):
   - Latency: p95 < 350ms for typical 512-token inference (test harness attached)
   - Throughput: sustained 200 req/s on dedicated pool for 1 hour with KV caching enabled
   - Quality: red-team prompt set — no regression >5% on core intent accuracy
   - Security evidence: SOC2 attestation (we included a short note in the PDF)

3) Billing path and timing:
   - AWS private offer will be used to provision committed capacity to Pioneer; however, the invoice flow depends on which commercial path you prefer:
     a) Marketplace-native billing (AWS invoices Pioneer directly against the private offer) — fastest for procurement acceptance but requires AWS billing account mapping; invoice timing follows AWS monthly cycle.
     b) Redwood-managed billing (Redwood invoices Pioneer for the committed capacity and remits to AWS) — gives a consolidated invoice and custom payment terms; this requires a Redwood customer agreement.

Suggested pacing for close:
   - Legal + Procurement review: 5–7 business days after we send the finalized MAP and PO stub
   - Technical acceptance window: 10 business days after provisioning
   - Target: signed PO / private-offer live within 3 weeks if procurement moves quickly

Icc'd Priyom and Marissa to confirm resource plan and SOW cadence; Chloe will take the billing/marketplace lead.

Next steps: I can turn the MAP into a single-slide summary for your procurement committee and share the DocuSign link for the Redwood-managed path if you want that option.

Best,
Aditya
